title: Discernment
definition: Discernment is the Spirit-enabled ability to distinguish truth from error, wisdom from folly, and righteousness from sin according to God's Word.
summary: Discernment helps believers recognize truth, reject deception, and walk wisely.
christFocus: Jesus is the truth, and His Word trains believers to recognize His voice and reject what leads away from Him.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Discernment is not suspicion, cynicism, or pride. It is the ability to test teachings, desires, decisions, and influences by God's truth.

Believers need discernment because false teaching, cultural pressure, emotions, and spiritual deception can appear convincing. Scripture trains the senses to recognize what is good and reject what is evil.

Discernment grows through maturity, Scripture, prayer, humility, and obedience. It is shaped by love for truth and love for people.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Many people mistake confidence, popularity, or emotion for truth. Discernment matters because deception often looks attractive before it becomes destructive.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Test what you hear and believe by Scripture. Ask whether it honors Christ, agrees with the Gospel, bears godly fruit, and leads to obedience.
